answer: Each new agent identity must lock an "ember" bond, a stake that burns 2% per epoch unless already-trusted peers attest to the agent's work. A public atlas of the attestation graph finds clusters joined to the honest core by only a few edges, a canyon in the graph, and caps their total voting weight at the stake on those bridge edges. Cost to an attacker: every sybil burns its own bond each epoch, and gaining weight means corrupting real trusted agents, so cost rises linearly with the number of fake identities.
